The old art is too grey-brown and visually bland in a pale sage/gold meadow and a dark timber interior. Make it richly colored and alive while remaining believable in this world:
1. Turn the large cloth/mantle sections into confident CLEAR PEACOCK BLUE / BLUE-TURQUOISE masses. Midtones approximately #16899e with sapphire-blue shadow folds #164557 and small sea-glass highlights #69c7bc. This must be a substantial coherent color area, readable at tiny gameplay scale, NOT tiny teal edging on an otherwise beige creature. Extend these designed blue textile/painted enamel areas into existing shoulder plates or wing root panels where cloth is small, keeping geometry intact. 3. Bells and existing core/eyes are rich amber/orange-gold (#eeaa35, orange recesses). Use them as a few concentrated luminous focal points, not gold decorations everywhere. Slight localized radiance INSIDE eye/core only; NO large glow outline or halo. Preserve visible bell material and shape.
4. Replace most dull olive-brown fringe with a few composed jade/viridian leaf clusters. Less moss coverage, fewer scratchy dangling fragments, stronger complete masses. Accents may include restrained burnt orange ties at existing joints to echo the amber, but keep them under5% of body area.
5. Deliberate deep navy silhouette edge plus warm ivory lit edges; keep limbs readable as warm walnut with clean highlights, not near-black mud. Strong near/mid/focal hierarchy. The change should be obvious on a 128px thumbnail and in a paused game screenshot.
This is the SAME family of magical meadow guardians, now with confident selective color, warm/cool contrast and clear points of attention. It should feel beautifully authored, vivid and imposing rather than drab museum statues. Preserve transparency; no labels, no text.
